rfis.subject: Unit Type A Compliance
rfis.question: Please confirm the requirements of a Type A unit. Sheet A5.0 includes a Bathroom Accessibility Matrix that designates, for each unit, whether Bathroom 1 and Bathroom 2 are Type A, Type B. Our understanding is that a “Type A” unit requires only one bathroom to carry the full Type A accessible package (clear floor/turning space, offset shower controls, ADA-height vanity with removable front, and grab bar reinforcement). Our confusion comes from the detailed bathroom elevations on Sheets A5.3-A5.5 show similarly detailed accessible features - including offset shower controls, grab bar reinforcement, and ADA clearance callouts - in both Bathroom 1 and Bathroom 2 for these units (e.g., "Bathroom 1 Elevation (Unit X02)" and "Bathroom 2 Elevation (Unit X02)" on Sheet A5.3, and similarly for unit types X03/X04). It's not clear from the elevations alone whether the second bathroom, i.e. Bath 2, in Units 206, 302, 403, 605 and 706 units are actually deemed to be installed to the lesser Type B clearances, or whether it was inadvertently drawn to the same Type A standard as Bath 1. Please confirm: Whether the second bathroom “Bath 2” in units 206, 302, 403, and other Type A units with a Type B second bathroom need to confirm with Type A requirements. Can you please confirm grab bars are not required to be installed at time of occupancy, rather be installed is tenant requests them in a Type A bathroom.

rfis.subject: Elevator Hoistway Venting
rfis.question: TKE has asked us to confirm whether the existing vent at the top of the elevator hoistway is required to remain, or whether it can be sealed as part of the elevator work. Please confirm the code requirement and direct how the top of the shaft should be detailed. Please reference TKE's Pre-Install Checklist (attached). Our understanding of the code: 1. The current Chicago Building Code (Title 14B) adopts the 2018 IBC by reference (14B-1-001). The hoistway venting requirement from older editions of the IBC (former Section 3004) was deleted from the 2018 edition, and Chicago's amendments in Chapter 14B-30 (Conveyance Devices) do not reinstate it. There is no requirement for a vent at the top of an elevator hoistway for new work. 2. For the change of occupancy from office (Group B) to residential (Group R-2), Chapter 14R-10 of the Chicago Rehabilitation Code governs. Section 1011.7 addresses elevator shafts strictly in terms of enclosure and opening protection (1011.7.3, 1011.7.4.1, 1011.7.5) - it does not require hoistway venting. Based on the above, our understanding is that the existing vent is a legacy condition from the original code and is not required to remain; it can be sealed, s ubject to your confirmation and any detailing on the permit drawings. Please confirm our understanding is correct, or advise otherwise. If you concur, please advise whether sealing the existing vent needs to be documented on the drawings, and provide any detail TKE needs to close out the top of the shaft. Given TKE's schedule recovery efforts, a response by end of week would be appreciated.
